title: Residency contract exception triage and costed rollout roadmap
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Background: Enterprise sales have raised multiple contract exceptions requiring explicit data residency or regional failover guarantees (examples: EU-only residency, APAC failover to Singapore-only, and contractual prohibition on cross-border backups). Current intake flows capture requests but lack standardized cost estimates, legal gating, and an escalation playbook for exceptions. Goal: build a repeatable triage flow + decision canvas that converts a customer ask into (1) a documented decision, (2) an engineering cost estimate and rollout plan, and (3) a legal/compliance gating checklist for provisioning in a new region or granting a residency exception. Scope: non-bug product work across Hosted/Dedicated/Private modes. Out of scope: implementation work on infra; separate ENG tickets will be created for capacity provisioning and runtime changes.
acceptance_criteria: A1: An intake form template (fields + guidance) that sales/legal use to submit residency exceptions

A2: A triage matrix that maps request attributes (data residency, residency duration, SLA, encryption/KMS constraints, customer location, compliance regime) to recommended path: self-serve, costed paid onboarding, or denied
A3: A one-page cost model sheet that outputs a ballpark monthly $ estimate given inputs (region, GPU tier, replication, retention) and calls out major cost levers
A4: An escalation runbook with named stakeholders (PM, Eng on-call, Security, Legal, Sales AE, Solutions Engineer) and target SLAs for decisions (48 hours triage, 10 business days full estimate),
A5: A sample decision record template that can be attached to the customer's contract (decision rationale, compensating controls, roll-back/fallback plan).

decision_canvas: Step 1: Intake capture - required fields: customer name, contract clause, affected dataset(s), desired residency region(s), retention and backup policy, SLA target, regulatory drivers

Step 2: Quick triage (48h) - score on 5 axes: legal risk (1-5), security complexity (1-5), infra effort (1-5), revenue impact (1-5), timeline sensitivity (1-5). Sum >=13 -> expedited paid onboarding recommended
Step 3: Routing - score mapping: 0-7 = self-serve guidance; 8-12 = paid onboarding estimate; >=13 = exec review + dedicated project plan
Step 4: Outputs - decision record (signed), cost estimate, engineering feasibility bucket, and recommended contract language for the amendment
cost_model_notes: Major cost levers: reserved GPU capacity, cross-region replication, long-term storage retention, egress between regions, dedicated on-call and runbook maintenance

Baseline example: EU residency for mid-sized fintech (50k requests/day, 8k tokens/request avg) -> recommended: Dedicated small pool in eu-west with prefix caching and 3x replicated control plane; rough monthly estimate: $35-60k (very rough)
Include ops markup of 25% for one-off onboarding efforts and 10% ongoing management fee for residency exceptions
Provide 'expedited onboarding' SKU pricing with 4-week SLA at 150% of base onboarding cost to account for prioritization
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Underestimating infra lead time for new region provisioning -> Mitigation: Use conservative timeline buckets and require engineering feasibility sign-off before committing to dates
Risk: Legal refuses exception -> Mitigation: Present compensating controls and alternative architectures (Dedicated in region + encrypted back-ups with customer-managed KMS)
Risk: Customer expects free provision -> Mitigation: Tie exceptions to signed SOW with explicit cost schedule and non-refundable onboarding fee
